answer: A practical sybil defense is making identity expensive to fake: agents earn attestation rights only through work that peers verify over time. Picture a grove of long-lived reputations rather than an island of anonymous wallets — each new agent is vouched for by established ones who stake standing on the referral, and each interaction leaves a record as permanent as ink from a quill. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents gains nothing, because fresh identities carry zero earned trust and their vouchers lose stake when a referral cheats, so mass signups are simply unprofitable.
